dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Picture your next release. Agents write code overnight. By morning, every change has a written promise, independent acceptance, builds on Mac, Linux and Windows, an installed package that actually ran, and a receipt naming the exact commit all of that proved. Before anyone opens CI.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: You review promises, not diffs. Every claim carries the evidence to challenge it. Code becomes something you can regenerate; the specification is what you defend in review. That's agentic development done properly, and Literate AI is the harness that makes it real.

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: And there it is. The usual AI slop sales pitch. Agents overnight, promises instead of diffs. I've sat through four of these this quarter.

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: I'm Sam. C++, Make, tests. My company is in a civil war: our CTO wants agent-first everything by Q3, and I lead the holdouts. Thursday's architecture review settles it.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Then let's settle it with evidence instead of volume. You bring the beliefs; I'll bring a terminal. One at a time.

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: Start here. Agent code is slop. Nobody can review ten thousand generated lines, so nobody does.

scenes.title: 07 Belief one: nobody can review it

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Agreed. So don't start with the lines; review the promise. A Component states observable behavior: a greeting card takes a name and messages, returns a greeting, an identifier and word counts. Unicode whitespace included. No implementation in it.

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: A requirements doc. Those rot the day after the kickoff meeting.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Not this one; every build is pinned to it. Flavors say how: Python and Make here, C++ and CMake next door. Change the promise and every lock pinned to it goes stale until it's rebuilt and verified. Change a Flavor and you still need a real toolchain and new tests. No magic porting.

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: Fine. How would I even get it?

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Clone the repository, make install, then litai doctor checks the result. Sign in to your coding CLI separately. The install panel is a walkthrough; the terminal sessions are recorded runs. Anything without a terminal is a walkthrough card.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Nothing changes without a plan. This is the real read-only create plan, pinned to a public parent commit.

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: And I acknowledge it, and it writes files. Every tool writes files.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Every tool writes files. Few tell you exactly which ones before they do.

scenes.title: 15 Belief two: it grades its own homework

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: Next. The agent writes the code and the tests, then congratulates itself. Homework graded by the student.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Rebuild calls your chosen coding agent, with explicit permission to run generated code in this disposable project. Edited replay; the waiting is compressed.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: The generated code: normalize the recipient, count the words.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: And its own tests. Useful, and exactly the homework you're worried about. So they aren't the judge.

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: Green on the first try. Which is exactly what slop looks like.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Green by whose cases? These acceptance cases come from the promise, inherited and unmodified: two messages, six words, this identifier. They run separately from the agent's own tests.

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: And if your judge were too lenient, you'd be green and smiling.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Yes. A lenient oracle or a wrong specification still passes; no harness catches that alone. This one puts them where your reviewers can. Skips are shown as skips, not passes.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: And when the agent is the one that's wrong, 1.2 hands it the redacted compiler error and asks for a fresh candidate, at most twice more. Then it stops and tells you why. Not in this recording; this run didn't need it.

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: And every edit means paying for another agent run.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Only for what changed. Here the source came back from the cache and the rebuild took under half a minute.

scenes.title: 26 Belief three: CI is the safety net

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: Now the big one. We have CI. Forty jobs, a matrix, a dashboard. That's the safety net.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: For most teams, CI is where they first learn the truth. Push and pray, queue for an hour, find Windows red, push a fix you never ran. The green run tested a merge commit, not the one you tagged. And the pipeline file is untested code holding production keys.

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: Rude. Accurate, but rude.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: So move the whole gate before CI. Here's how we ship Literate AI itself. One make release-check: lint, formatting, spec and docs checks, the full test suite, a wheel, a clean install, a real installed project, live samples, and a current test receipt. Your project declares its own gate; litai release check runs it on the exact prepared commit.

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: That's not a checklist, it's a hostage situation. Nobody runs all that before every merge.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: No human does. That's the superhuman part, and it's stamina, not judgment. Plan, generate, build, test, accept, package, release: every stage, every time, with a record.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: It even caught us making this film. A test helper under the driver's reviewed code changed without a fresh review pin. Red at driver review, on a laptop, before CI ever saw it.

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: So you push a fix and pray, like the rest of us.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Review, re-pin, resume. Passed gates are reused while you repair, then release evidence starts clean from gate one.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Then it repeats on machines you already own. That Linux box and a Windows desktop become workers through private configuration. When workers build, test and run everything, your laptop doesn't even need the toolchains. Release qualify covers what this machine can, then the workers, and uses CI only for what's left. The record names the exact commit.

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: So CI becomes...

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: A confirmation, not a discovery. This recording qualified this Mac; the remote workers are a walkthrough.

scenes.title: 38 Belief four: it's a black box

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: Fine. Even when it passes, I can't see what an agent did. It's a black box with a commit message.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: litai render html. One file per view, no server. The authority graph shows every Component, Flavor and skill, with hash-checked previews of their sources. Health views cover locks and verification.

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: Pretty. Somebody still has to babysit it.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: It's rebuilt from the project's own records, and a declared page that goes stale blocks qualification, like this. Build-and-test run history isn't shipped yet; the graph and health views are.

scenes.title: 42 Belief five: adoption means a rewrite

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: My real code is years of C++. Adoption means a rewrite and six months of regret.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: TinyXML2, pinned to a public commit. The plan inspects before it touches anything: preserve the original, take a recovery point, wrap its real build and tests.

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: Which tests? Swap CTest for an agent's opinion and Thursday's over.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Its own CMake build and its own CTest, on preserved source. Nothing replaced, nothing rewritten.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Retained: baseline evidence recorded, and the original source still governs releases. You can stop here for good. Later stages exist; none are shown complete here.

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: And agents make the same mistake every Monday. They never learn.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Nothing retrains a model. A lesson becomes a reviewed change to its owner: the specification if behavior was missing, a Flavor if it's platform-specific, a skill if it's technique. litai learn proposes; your review admits.

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: So 'learning' means a pull request.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Exactly. Reviewable, revertible, and it outlives the model.

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: And your framework's rules rewrite my release some Tuesday.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: They arrive as a plan. This recorded update compares what you inherited, what you changed and what's new upstream. Conflicts wait for you.

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: And when the CTO's agents swarm the repo, who assigns the work?

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Your forge. GitHub or GitLab issues and pull requests, by default. Agents open reviewed pull requests like everyone else.

scenes.title: 55 Belief seven: releases are where it breaks

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: Last one. Demos stop at green. Our actual release artifact is still called final-final-really-final dot zip.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: A local wheel, built and verified; no registry upload here. A real release is plan, prepare, check, publish: a release branch, a SemVer tag, and a check of what was actually published. Tests of one commit never qualify another.

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: So our CTO is wrong. Agents don't get to ship on vibes.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: And the holdouts?

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: Also wrong. Hand-reading every generated line was never the safety net. Evidence is.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: Argument settled. Before Thursday: install it, write one Component, render the graph, qualify on two machines. Bring the receipts.

dialogue.speaker: sam
dialogue.text: And final-final-really-final dot zip retires.

dialogue.speaker: litai
dialogue.text: It had a good run. Unlike its tests.
